market_view: The Nasdaq fell 1.25% on the FT report that OpenAI's annualized revenue is about $20B below earlier figures, which hit semis hardest, while the 10-year near 5.2% and Brent above $103 cap multiples. Futures are flat tonight, so I'm favoring company-specific catalysts (Barclays' A&D initiation, CMS star ratings, SpaceX's spectrum deal) over broad AI beta.
lessons: Nine positions were stopped in one session. The 3-4% stops on high-beta AI and semis names (MU, AVGO, BE, INTC, TSM) all hit on a single sector-wide scare, so on these names I'm now using stops of at least 5-6% and not stacking several picks on the same AI theme.

All four read-through and pre-print small-cap moonshots failed. CIFR and CORZ, bought as sympathy plays on APLD's beat, faded at the open, and ANGO and TLRY fell after their prints. Moonshots now need a company-specific catalyst, not a peer's news.

Buying into a print when expectations are depressed worked: PEP bounced 3.2% off its 52-week low on the beat, and LW's beat-and-raise drift is up 3%. Low bars plus confirmed timing beat chasing momentum.

review.reason: Post-earnings drift is working (+3%, closed near the high), so I'm keeping the 51.6 target and raising the stop to just under entry to protect the gain.

Q3 is reported before Friday's open against estimates already cut to about $1.76-1.83. The fuel part of my thesis is weaker with Brent above $103, but a SELL would also exit at the post-print open, so I'm keeping the print exposure with the existing stop.
Flat and held up on a tech-led down day; the Oct 13 pre-market print is still inside the hold window.
The OpenAI revenue report hits the AI-capex narrative, but it reflects accounting presentation, not a demand cut. With a 60-day horizon and the stop 8% below, I'm keeping the core holding.
Flat since entry; the valuation and TPU/Cloud thesis are intact.
Down 1.5% with the tech tape and no company-specific negative; thesis intact into late-October earnings.
Down 1% on the AI selloff with no change to the AWS and advertising thesis.
Still positive and holding relative strength through the healthcare and tech weakness; thesis intact.
The beat lifted it 3.2% despite a trimmed core EPS outlook. On its last session I'm keeping the 131 target and raising the stop above entry to lock in a gain.

moonshot.thesis: Barclays initiated A&D coverage after the close with Kratos at Overweight and a $90 target, more than double the $41.93 close. That follows BNP Paribas' upgrade to Outperform this morning and heavy call buying, with the stock sitting at its 52-week low (from $134). The new initiation lands at Friday's open.
moonshot.main_risk: Defense-tech is in a heavy downtrend, so initiations can get sold into; a broader AI/tech selloff would drag it below the 52-week low.

moonshot.thesis: Barclays initiated Rocket Lab at Overweight with an $85 target, 24% above the $68.40 close, citing launch cadence and space components. The stock fell 4.9% Thursday and was flat after hours before the note circulated, so the reaction is still ahead.
moonshot.main_risk: The SPCX lockup expiry on Oct 9 could weigh on space names, and a weak tech tape could swamp the initiation.

moonshot.thesis: Two Street calls in one day: Goldman upgraded to Buy ($230) this morning, then Barclays initiated at Overweight with a $265 target tonight. PLTR rose 2.4% on a day the Nasdaq fell 1.25%, and it closed at $198.78, 4% below its $207.52 all-time high, so a breakout attempt is set up.
moonshot.main_risk: A rich valuation in an AI tape spooked by the OpenAI revenue report; sellers could defend the all-time high.

moonshot.thesis: CMS's 2027 star ratings, released after the close, gave Clover's PPO plans covering about 98% of members 5 stars, the top rating and above-bonus-threshold economics for 2028. Shares are up 4-7% after hours to about $4.76-4.90 on a $4.58 close, and Clover argues the litigated measures would have scored even higher.
moonshot.main_risk: The stock is already up about 95% YTD and the 52-week high is $5.59, so sell-the-news after the gap is possible.

moonshot.thesis: SpaceX agreed after the close to buy Grain Management's nationwide 800 MHz low-band spectrum for a hybrid ground-plus-space Starlink Mobile network. That deal marks a fresh value for low-band spectrum near NextNav's 900 MHz position. NN fell 8.7% to $11.60 Thursday and rebounded 3-7% after hours, with 15% of the float short.
moonshot.main_risk: The read-through is my inference and no source ties NN's after-hours move to the deal; NextNav's 900 MHz plan still needs FCC action.

catalyst.thesis: TSMC's September revenue of NT$511.9B was up 54.6% y/y (Jan-Sep +41.1%), yet the ADR fell 3% to $457.99 in the OpenAI-driven semis selloff. Q3 results land Oct 15 at 2am ET, inside a 5-session hold, so I'm positioning for a pre-print recovery.
catalyst.main_risk: The AI-capex scare deepens and drags all semis; geopolitical or tariff headlines.

catalyst.thesis: After the close, RTX won a multi-year SM-3 Block IB interceptor contract worth up to $6.3B, and Barclays initiated it at Overweight with a $223 target (21% upside from $184.32), citing defense backlog and engine aftermarket. Both land before Friday's open.
catalyst.catalyst_time: 2026-10-08 after close (contract award and Barclays initiation)
catalyst.main_risk: A low-beta mega-cap may not move much, and the contract may already be partly expected in the backlog.

catalyst.thesis: Barclays initiated Boeing at Overweight with a $300 target, 60% above the $187.75 close, near the $176.77 52-week low, on fleet-renewal demand and stabilizing production. Reuters also reports Southwest is leaning toward the 787 for its first widebody, a potential new order.
catalyst.main_risk: Production or quality headlines, and a weak industrial tape; the Southwest order isn't confirmed.

catalyst.thesis: SpaceX's 800 MHz purchase is to support a hybrid Starlink Mobile network serving customers 'from both the ground and space', a potential new terrestrial tenant for towers. Crown Castle jumped about 7-9% after hours to $73.6-75.0 on more than $200M of after-hours dollar volume from a $68.89 close, near its 52-week low after a slide from $100.
catalyst.main_risk: The tower-tenant link is inferred, not stated by SpaceX. If the gap fades the stop sits below the prior close, and weaker carriers (T, VZ, TMUS down 7%) are towers' main customers.

catalyst.thesis: Wells Fargo reports Q3 on Oct 13 at 7am ET, inside a 3-session hold, after TD Cowen resumed it at Buy on Oct 8 (shares +2.2% to $82.03). With M&A and trading strong and the asset cap gone, it trades 16% below its $97.76 high, so I'm positioning for a pre-print run-up.
catalyst.main_risk: The reported HUD probe into its homeownership programs and an earnings miss; it's correlated with my JPM position.
